# [PEN-3329](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/PEN/issues/PEN-3329)

**Files:** `src/server/shared-doc-overlay.ts` (new), `src/server/shared-doc-overlay.test.ts` (new), `src/server/job-manifest.ts`, `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`

Carries the shared docs an agent's `AGENTS.md` tells it to read into a **run-isolated**
pod. Paperclip materializes those docs (`docs/<name>.md`) into the execution workspace
server-side, before the Job is created, on the premise — stated in
`materializeExternalK8sSharedDocs`' own comment — that "these adapters mount (or clone)
this local execution workspace into the pod, so writes here are visible remotely". The
mount half holds. **The clone half does not:** `workspaceSetup` bootstraps with `git clone
--shared --no-checkout` + `checkout --detach`, and a clone carries **tracked objects
only**, while the materialized docs are untracked by construction — Paperclip even appends
them to the base's `info/exclude` so the workspace does not read as dirty. Not one of them
crosses. Measured on the live `penstock-llm-proxy-core` base checkout 2026-10-29: **all 14**
referenced docs untracked, so all 14 absent from any clone of it.

Two bootstrap branches, one cause, and the second is the one that looks like a different
bug. When the source cwd is not a repository, `workspaceSetup` takes its `else` branch —
`rm -rf` + `mkdir -p` — and the pod's cwd is an **empty directory, not a clone at all**.
That is the shape the CEO read first-person on 2026-10-29 (`ls -a` → `. ..`, `git
rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` → `fatal: not a git repository`) and reasonably flagged as
not matching PEN-3329's stated `--shared`-clone mechanism. It is the same `if`. The step
added here runs after `fi`, so it covers both; a test pins the empty-directory branch
specifically.

The set is **declared, not discovered**: the server reports the exact paths on
`context.paperclipSharedDocs` and the pod copies those. Copying `docs/` wholesale was
rejected — it would overwrite the clone's *tracked* docs with the base checkout's
working-tree copies, and the base is long-lived and may sit on another branch entirely.

Four properties are load-bearing and each has a test:

- **Never overwrites.** `[ -e ]` short-circuits per path, so a tracked doc keeps the cloned
  revision's content. This fills absences only.
- **Never fails the run.** Missing source, unwritable destination and read-only `.git` are
  each reported on stderr and stepped over; the step ends `true` so a reported failure
  cannot become its exit code. Documentation must not be able to fail a pod.
- **Re-excludes what it copies.** The clone gets a fresh `.git`, so the base's
  `info/exclude` entries do not come with it, and without re-adding them a broad `git add
  -A` would commit all 14 docs into the agent's PR — BLO-22984's failure re-created one
  layer down. `isSafeSharedDocPath` rejects every character git's exclude syntax reads as a
  pattern (`* ? [ ] \ ! #`), which is what lets the entry be appended unescaped; a test
  pins that coupling so widening the charset reddens rather than silently breaking it.
- **States its verdict.** Absence and placeholder content are both named in the pod log.
  This is why the check cannot be "assert no `# Missing Shared Documentation` heading": that
  passes against a file which is simply **absent**, which is exactly the failure here.
  PEN-3172's Done-when was written that way and would have reported success.

Path handling is re-validated at this boundary (`docs/`-anchored, `.md`, no `..`, no
absolute, no leading `-`) rather than trusted from the context, and unsafe entries are
dropped individually instead of failing the overlay.

Verified end-to-end against a real `git clone --shared` of a real repo driven by a real
`/bin/sh`, including a test that reproduces the defect itself (the clone carrying the
tracked doc and neither untracked one) so the suite cannot go green against a bug that has
moved. Mutation-checked per the BLO-34263 rule: deleting the splice from the pod command
reddens two manifest tests in each tree.
